subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment and scope rules should it use relative to user-token `search.messages` work?
rationale: The requested capability is valid but security-sensitive: it handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, and current overlapping work uses a different legacy/user-token search API.

options.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate with user-token search
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers both RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then update the overlapping PR or a replacement PR to match it.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack search out of core until maintainers are ready to own the token/privacy/scope model and live validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack assistant lifecycle, action-runtime, action discovery, docs, and the overlapping action-parity PR all route through this contributor's history.
